title: Attainment of the decision-tree depth
statement: Let $f \colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables, and let $d$ be its decision-tree depth. Then there exists a decision tree $T$ of depth at most $d$ that computes $f$, meaning $T$ evaluated at $x$ equals $f(x)$ for every input $x$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on Fin n → Bool
replaced:
For any Boolean function $f$ there exists a decision tree $T$ computing $f$ with
depth at most $\mathrm{dtDepth}\,f$.
